Tasks: 84 core + 29 debugging tasks, scored separately. Configurations: 13 models with one scaffold. Baseline: none (null arm, a do-nothing agent, used only to validate checks). Held constant: system prompt, tools, 300 s time budget, 200 tool-call budget, 16 attempts, engine version; reasoning effort high; sampling set per family. Acceptance: hand-written executable checks validated against reference solutions. Repetitions: 16 attempts per task; infrastructure failures relaunched, timeouts scored as failures. Human intervention: none. Runs May-July 2026

Top five models within 1.1 pp (50.6-51.7% pass@1); paired tests separate 34 of 78 model pairs (15 after Holm). Top five: union of solved tasks 58, intersection 27 (placebo 47/37). Spread among top five 5.0 pp on script-authoring, 12.5 pp on scene-change, 13.1 pp on debugging. Consistency gap about 31 points from pass@5 to all@5. Coverage from none to full: +13.4 pp on scene-only (95% CI [+1.2, +25.7]) and +9.8 pp on script-only ([+3.6, +16.0]); difference between arms not significant (p = 0.59)

Paired comparisons and placebo baselines distinguish models that average similar rates; 16 attempts allow reliability metrics; minimum detectable effect 9.2 pp for the median pair. Limitations: system prompt and hosted runtime not released; single engine and language; coverage needs annotations; IRT on only 13 models

Single engine and language (Luau); exploration proxy tied to the eight-tool action space; coverage depends on manual dependency annotation; text-only agents (no visual feedback); checks may be wrong (screened; null arm passes 5 tasks); scripted, not model-driven play-time checks; system prompt and runtime not open; contamination risk (no consistent evidence found). Future: automatic dependency derivation
